checks.rationale: AC2 passes: shared immutable inputs, logical-reference constructor parity, and typed failure paths are supported. AC1 and AC3 fail on two reproduced digest defects: objective prose can change without invalidating approval, while a known task bucket directory scope reference cannot relocate without changing identity. All 27 v1 kinds, strict unknown fields, current bootstrap digest parity, and installed transitive closure have positive evidence.

Frozen flat-module boundaries and specification exclusions are respected, with no provider, schema, canonical-state, or later CLI wiring changes. However the requirement that structural changes invalidate approval is violated by the confirmed objective-prose digest collision, and lifecycle-neutral scope references are incomplete.

Traced the closed registry, schema dispatch, typed exception translation, deduplicated live bundle discovery, strict graph digest comparison, and AST import closure. The validator correctly compares hashes but the digest projection loses a structural prose distinction and retains a physical directory distinction; an approved-graph fixture confirms the resulting stale approval is accepted.

Unsupported version/kind, schema shape, invalid logical references, unavailable offline resources, and broken local references map to declared nonretryable DomainException categories; foundation preserves its ValidationFailure CLI boundary. Schema file reads are scoped, installer planning discovers missing modules before payload writes, subprocess fixtures use argument lists, and temporary fixtures clean up. No resource leak was found in the changed paths.

Immutable JSON and detached schema views, bare/cross-plan reference rejection, all provider roots and both separators, completed/archived record paths, and cyclic transitive imports are addressed. Path-prefixed prose and exact known lifecycle bucket directory claims remain uncovered incorrect edge cases.

The exact-candidate evidence records 16 meaningful focused tests, including malformed/offline references, frozen values, schema-view mutation, live artifact discovery, installed imports from an unrelated cwd, relocation, and stale-scope rejection. Handoff records 24 bootstrap tests and foundation checks; R1 did not repeat them. The digest tests nevertheless miss the two decisive acceptance cases reproduced independently, so regression coverage is insufficient for AC1/AC3 until those cases are added.

Independent Git scope reconstruction finds only contracts.py, validate_foundation.py, the bounded install.py closure update, task-owned schema tests, and task handoff. The installer follows canonical flat imports and does not alter seeds, native provider settings, or later lifecycle/release behavior. ai.py remains unchanged under TASK-034 ownership.

Exact base/head binary diff and fingerprint match the frozen candidate; all context, validation, and policy/model hashes match. The five changed paths are permitted, with no renames, deletions, unrelated edits, or dirty candidate files. The accepted TASK-001 candidate is an ancestor of the review base and r4 graph/task digests still match isolation approval.

Public registry, reference parser, and digest functions are explicit flat-module interfaces using accepted shared values/errors. Defensive schema copies and frozen input conversion maintain separation; installer dependency discovery is compact and handles cycles. The two reported defects require bounded normalization repairs rather than a new abstraction or public contract change.

The registry has no remote retrieval callback, unavailable resource targets fail closed, unknown fields/versions are rejected, plan-local references require qualification, and the change adds no external effects. However an objective mutation can reuse the same approved graph/review digest, violating the structural approval trust boundary. No alternate stale-hash fallback exists; the collision arises in canonicalization.

The task handoff accurately identifies scope, public interfaces, standalone helper closure, test commands, prior diagnostics, later CLI ownership, and native provenance limits. Its assertions that prose is not rewritten and lifecycle locations are neutral are too broad in light of the two reproduced defects. Update the handoff alongside the bounded fixes and retain failed-cycle history.

findings.description: At src/contracts.py:357 every structural string is passed through a prefix-only location expression. Changing objective prose from '.codex/plans/current/PLAN-101/spec.json must remain the selected active specification.' to the completed-path sentence produces the same digest. Both records are schema-valid, and an independent fresh installed-project fixture confirms validate_foundation accepts the changed objective under the unchanged approved graph and isolation review. A substantive objective change can therefore retain stale approval.
findings.expected_fix: Restrict lifecycle normalization to recognized path values and preserve prose as structural text; do not normalize a string merely because it begins with a rooted record-path fragment. Keep bootstrap projection/encoding compatibility, add a regression proving the changed objective invalidates an approved graph, and correct the handoff claim. Do not accept stale hashes as fallback.

findings.description: At src/contracts.py:62 the task-location regex requires TASK-NNN after the bucket. The legitimate directory-prefix scope read path '.codex/plans/current/PLAN-101/tasks/current/' and its relocated '.codex/plans/completed/PLAN-101/tasks/completed/' form consequently hash differently. These are exact known provider-root, plan-qualified task lifecycle bucket directory claims supported by accepted TASK-001 ScopePath semantics, not arbitrary embedded paths. This violates r4 AC3 and the frozen lifecycle-neutral scope digest invariant and makes an unchanged relocated scope stale.
findings.expected_fix: Canonicalize recognized task lifecycle bucket directory-prefix scope paths as well as known task record paths. Preserve exact current-location bootstrap encoding, exclude arbitrary embedded paths/prose, and add regression coverage showing directory-only relocation preserves approval while a real scope change invalidates it. Update the handoff and retain strict digest equality without stale-hash fallback.
